The **DMPG-retningslinje** (DMPG guideline) is a professional clinical guideline focused on the non-pharmacological treatment of ADHD in Denmark. It serves as a normative reference for quality measurement and improvement within the national ADHD care system. The guideline is particularly significant because the [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]] (Steering Committee) has decided to adopt it to guide its ongoing work with national quality indicators [^src1]. 

In the context of the 2024 national ADHD report, the DMPG-retningslinje is directly linked to the development and implementation of specific quality metrics. For [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which measures psychoeducation, the steering group plans to use the upcoming DMPG guideline for non-pharmacological ADHD treatment to inform its future work and address systemic implementation challenges [^src1]. Furthermore, the guideline's framework extends to [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]], a new quality metric for adult ADHD care that assesses social support needs within 120 days of treatment initiation. In this area, the DMPG-retningslinje is referenced regarding future work on "social screening" and data definitions, highlighting its role in shaping clinical assessment practices [^src2].

Overall, the DMPG-retningslinje bridges the gap between clinical guidelines and national quality databases, ensuring that both non-pharmacological interventions and social support assessments are standardized across Danish psychiatric departments.
